scope: Direct QNN ASR ownership, partial construction and checked retirement; exact production-source host failure injection and Android arm64 API/object compilation. No model inference or physical accelerator qualification.
changes: Admit process-owned Session before native model acquisition; retain fully constructed shared QNN states before initialization can throw.
Retire metadata/context/power/device/backend/logger in dependency order. First uncertain free retains all remaining owners and seals new admission; it cannot be retried.
Keep QNN model mappings, metadata, tensors and libraries through confirmed retirement, including failed constructor rollback without a returned Java handle.
Null outputs on failed creation permit cleanup of only earlier confirmed acquisitions. Non-null outputs accompanying an error remain quarantined because their valid ownership is unconfirmed.
Reject successful power-client creation returning zero before changing process-global settings; never destroy the global/NULL id.
JNI waits for the session mutex and erases only after checked retirement succeeds. Healthy sessions can independently retire after another session seals new admission.
Java and Kotlin clear native handles only after successful close. A failed/no-handle constructor rollback remains an explicit close failure consumed by the existing model-lease quarantine.
ASR NPU model loading accepts pinned context binaries only and fails if a binary disappears instead of attempting upstream model-SO fallback.
Host-only CTest regression compiles the actual patched QNN classes against a deterministic C ABI fixture; Android production targets do not include the fixture.
